timecoded_text_to_speech.text: It fascinates me how things work, not just why things work.
It's like with a lightbulb. We all know that it lights up, but not everyone knows how it lights up.
And that's sort of what I try to hear through my pictures.
I like showing pictures to my family because my pictures are sort of reflect who I am and what I like.
I'd always felt the moon was pretty, but I didn't really know anything about it.
I didn't really think that I'd be able to see the moon from our house, because it's quite open-minded.
It's hardly ever dark and you can't really see the sky very clearly.
I used to have a little digital compact camera, but I wanted a better one, so I saved all my Christmas money up.
And we bought it, and then I'd lost it.
It was really upsetting because it was like a loss to piece of me because I'd express myself through the pictures.
The picture made me look at the world in a better way, because it's not just houses and cars.
There is beautiful places out there near where you live. You just need to look a bit ahead.
To find out more about the competition and to see some of the beautiful images involved, visit the website.

The 2014 Astronomy Photographer of the Year Exhibition is now open at the Royal Observatory http://www.rmg.co.uk/astrophoto

Emily Jeremy was Highly Commended in our Young Astrophotographer category. Here she talks about her shot 'Moon Behind the Trees'.
